links.reason: Kural 549 says punishing wrongdoers is no fault (வடுவன்று); verse 140 faults the king for lacking grace to the lowly (கீழுயிர் மேலருளாமை). Neither denies the other, so there is no incompatible claim, and the note itself says the Kural does not ask for it.

Pur 35 says the umbrella is for the afflicted subjects (குடிமறைப்பதுவே) and cc 159 has it shade the world like a father (தாதையே). The contrast of warning and settled praise is real, but 'the story will soon need' the warning rests on plot outside the verse.

Kural 5 says deeds do not cling to those who praise the lord (புகழ்புரிந்தார் மாட்டு), not that deeds do not cling to the lord, so the note misreads the couplet. Verse 16 only names him who conquered deeds (வல்வினை வென்ற); reading the Kural in a Jain way is imposed.
1460 does list the body's marks (அடியிணை ஆமையின் வடிவு கொண்டன, விலா, கண்) and 1438 names the மெய்ப்பொறி body. That a stranger recognises a destined husband by them is not in either Tamil text.

243 says the learned keep off blame and fierce deeds (பழியும் வெய்ய வினைகளும் விலக்கி நின்றார் நூல்விளை புலவர்); 547 says justice guards the king if he does not falter. Naming counsellors is a real addition but a thin, generic one.

Both set gold seat and loss: 1476 asks whether the king of the golden bed should lie on an elephant's brow, 642 says the gold throne does not go with the body. The pairing teaches only the common theme of lost luxury; the 'gains' claims are thin.

664 has Kattiyankaran say only Kama could beat her at the vina and none such is here (காமனாகும் ... ஒழிக ஈங்கில்லை); 2335 calls the king's slayer வீணை வித்தகன். That is an irony fulfilled, not a tension.

The Akananuru wedding has sand-strewn pandal, lamps and garlands; cc 2391 orders plantain, areca, aloe pots, lute and flags. The parts differ, so 'same adornments grown in scale' is not what the Tamil shows.
1469 has 'வினைக்கள்வர் ஆறலைப்ப ... வெண்குணனும் கோட்பட்டு' and 1420 names the எண்வினை, so the pairing is plausible. The teaches line is only a statement that two hymns of one ilampakam go together.

908 has her say 'சீவகன் பொன்றும் சாகம் பொருந்திற் பொருந்துக ... ஒன்று சிந்தையளாகி', which can be read as a vow holding Civakan; patikam 13 says she looks on no male form (ஆண் உரு யாதும் நோக்காள்). The exception reading is plausible but needs a generous reading; sense uncertain.

3082 shows Civakan overcoming the destroying karmas by war (காதிப்போர் மன்னர் வீழ ... இறைமை கொண்டான்) while Tirumanthiram 113 has the Lord descend and cut the stain (களிம்பறுத்தானே). Self-won victory against grace-given cutting is a defensible incompatibility on whose act removes bondage.

695 has the minister say the prince lacks the sense to tell good from bad (நன்று தீது என்னும் தேர்ச்சி நவின்றிலன்) and plan a ruse; 636 is about keen wit with learning. The link rests on a loose analogy and 'gains' names no real lack.

1167 has 'காமக் கடும்புனல் நீந்தி ... யாமத்தும் யானே உளேன்' and 1663 'யாமக் கடலை நீந்துவேன் யாரும் இல்லாத் தமியேனே', with the women who laugh (பூமென் குழலார் ... நகுவார்) added. The epic adds a public, social side to the bare solitude.

1091 says he was bound by the word 'தோள் ஆண்மை குன்றாது' bound as in a seal (சொல் இமிழிற் பூட்டி); 1116 has him go 'சிலம்பி நூலாற் சிமிழ்ப்புண்ட சிங்கம்', the thread being that word. A later image fulfils the earlier binding.

29 says Civakan will not want women's pleasure (முலை போகம் வேண்டான்); 2477 shows the wedding night. Setting pleasure beside later renunciation is only a thematic contrast, and 'counts for more' is a claim the verses do not make.

Both have rags removed and clothing given: pattupattu 153-155 (சிதாஅர் நீக்கி ... பட்டுடை நல்கி), Pur 385 (சிதாஅர் களைந்து வெளியது உடீஇ). That this shows a recognised rite of reception is an inference neither text states.

1050 has her say that if father and mother do not agree there is death or penance (எந்தையும் யாயும் நேராராய்விடின்), so she is asking for her chosen man; the nurse's rich-cousin match is not in the verse. The Akananuru girl refuses a kin wedding, so the contrast rests on a reconstructed plot.

1860 asks for a refuge beyond Death (காலன் தன்னை நாம் இகந்து சேரும் சரண் பிறிது உரைமின்) and 1862 answers that there is no shelter but the ascetic's feet (செறிதவர் சரண ... அல்லால் அரண் பிறிது ஆவது உண்டோ). The later verse answers the earlier.

NKK 17 says he burned all old deeds (தொல்வினை எல்லாம் எரித்த); TM 117 says the sunstone burns the malas only in the sun's presence. A hymn of praise does not argue for effort over grace, so a real tension is not established, only a contrast of statements.

YK 80 has the fear that women will turn away at old age (மூப்பிது உண்டெனில் ... கண்டு அகலுற); Siddhar 809 spends youth on women and ends with a staff. The Tamil shown does not give Asokan reading the white hair, which the teaches relies on.

46 asks what is gained by going the outside way; Neelakesi 18 names those who leave the forest and stony troubles and strive to wear away deeds (செய்வினைகள் நைய முயல்வாரும்) beside the householders of gift and virtue (தானமொடு சீலம்). The poet gives a gain the household does not.

1243 and 1246 both have arrows darkening the sky (காரிருள் / இருண்டன). The note's claim that darkness shields the attackers and then blinds them is not in the Tamil; this is battle sequence, not tension.

2024 ranks beings best, middle, lowest by the fruit of ten kinds of virtue (பத்துவகை பாதவம் இயற்றிய பயத்தால்); Kural 37 points to rider and bearer. The ladder of births is not in the verse, so 'gains' is partly invented; the link illustrates.
526 has the king call all that was said a dream (கனவெனக் கருதினல்லான்); 106 tells a real dream (கனாக்கண்டது). Only the word 'dream' is shared; there is no conflicting claim.

1925 asks what use a stratagem is to a lion against a jackal (சூழ்ச்சி நற்றுணையொடு என்னாம்); 1928 has the cave lion who roars and leaps fall into the net. The second answers the boast, so it qualifies it rather than conflicts.

Naladiyar 1: those who ate six-flavoured food will go begging for gruel. 2941: those who ate rich food fear the begging (பிச்சை ஏற்றலால் அஞ்சினேன்). The same fall is the quatrain's reason to renounce and the speaker's reason to hesitate.

335 has the king worship after the teaching (பேர்ந்து வணங்கினன்) and gives sight (தெரிசனம்) as shedding deeds; so 'no worship is needed' is false. TM 219 burns deeds by the fire, but the opposition of means is overstated.

1844 says those who cut the root of good deeds become kings of hells (நரகங்கட்கு அரசராவார்); 1923 lists the layers and lakh of dwellings (எண்பஃதுடன் நான்கு). Kings are not in 1923, so 'room for every fallen king' is read in.
21 has peacocks dancing to the clouds' roar (ஆர்த்தொறும் ஆலும் மயில்); Akananuru 82 has the peacock dance as the hill's concert. The Akam is fuller, so 'epic gains a fuller account' is reversed.

Kalittokai 5 ends 'எந்நாளோ நீ செல்வது அந்நாள் கொண்டு இறக்கும் இவள் உயிரே' after the emptied festival ground and the lotus out of water (14-15), matching Kural 1151's 'செல்லாமை உண்டேல் எனக்குரை'. The poem is the full argument the couplet compresses.

Thiri 50 names king, liars and the woman crossing the house's bounds as the three that cut rain; cc 255 makes failed rain and lost chastity follow from the bent sceptre (அரசு கோல் கோடின்) with planets out of course (கோள் நிலை திரிந்து). The causal order differs and the கோள் reading holds.

14 has the cowherds' sweet flute at evening (கொன்றையந் தீங்குழல்); Akananuru 74 has her pained by the cowherds' flute (கோவலர் ஊதும் வல்வாய் சிறுகுழல் வருத்தாக் காலே). The shared flute is real, but the lesson that meaning depends on the hearer is generic.

3072 says he stood four months in the open cold cherishing the dear life (இன்னுயிர் ஓம்பினான்); TM 724 nurtures the body. The verse does not say he spent the body, so the opposition about what a body is for is read in.
1511 has 'நிழலின் நீப்பருங் காதலும் நீத்தியோ' (love inseparable as a shadow); 1524 has her speak to her own shadow as a friend (நிழல் ... அமர் தோழி). The simile becomes her situation.
323 has the voice from the branches say 'சீவ' (சினை மறைந்து ஒரு குரல் சீவ என்றதே); 361 names him சீவகன். The name carries the omen's word.

3022 has the feet that walked on the open lotus (விண்டலர் பூந்தாமரையின் ... மேல் நடந்த) and Kural 3 has 'மலர்மிசை ஏகினான்'. The image is shared, but the epic only illustrates the couplet and the Kural gains nothing real.

497 names fearlessness as the one help provided one weighs and acts by place (எஞ்சாமை எண்ணி இடத்தால் செயின்); 1925 has a speaker say a stratagem is no use to a lion. Who speaks and the mother's later verses are reconstructed plot; there is no shared run of words.

Kural 1311's wife says all women feast on him with their eyes (கண்ணின் பொதுஉண்பர்); 238 is Dattai's anger at his union with Manikai. They are different grievances, and the settling by her bowing is not in the verse.

290 has the minister-snake swallow Saccandan (மந்திரி மா நாகமுடன் விழுங்கிற்று); 2146 has a mad elephant kill and the sceptre slacken (கூற்றென முழங்கி வீழ்த்துக் கொல்ல). The two accounts differ, but that 2146 is the usurper's propaganda is reconstructed.

744 has Kattiyankaran say whoever beats him wins fortune (திருவினுக்கு உரியீர்); 755 says he means them to fight one another and then the king too (நும்முளே பொருது வீந்தால்). The reversal is real; that it repeats his method on Saccandan is not in the Tamil.

148 praises not looking on another's wife (பிறன்மனை நோக்காத பேராண்மை); in 1705 he looks at neither face, breasts nor waist but her anklet (சீறடிச் சிலம்பு நோக்கி). The scene adds the case where a man must meet and speak to her.

44 has Kanaiyan taken captive by the Chola (கணையன் அகப்படக்); 386 compares the lover's shame to Kanaiyan's (நற்போர்க் கணையன் நாணியாங்கு). That the poets used his name only for defeat is a generalisation from two poems and rests on the name alone.

409 has Tivittan split a lion's mouth within a month (திங்கள் நாள் அகவையில்); 607 repeats the prophecy as already said (தான் முன் சொன்னதே). It is a repetition of one prophecy, and 'two courts' is the note's inference.
